texts.li: The colony holds {COUNT} faiths now, and it shows. {A_nameDef} of {FAITH} and {B_nameDef} of {OTHERFAITH} both want the evenings for their own faith, and neither will give way. {WHY}\n\nThey have asked the council to settle it.

{B_nameDef} says {FAITH} behaves as if the colony were already theirs. {A_nameDef} says {OTHERFAITH} could share a little more gracefully. {WHY}\n\nWith {COUNT} faiths under one roof, the council is asked how they should live together.
[b:faith:devout] {B_nameDef} has stopped coming to meals when {A_nameDef} says the words of {FAITH} over them. {WHY}\n\nThe council is asked to find a way for {COUNT} faiths to share one colony.
[lowtech] There is one fire to gather at, and {COUNT} faiths that want it. {A_nameDef} speaks for {FAITH}, {B_nameDef} for {OTHERFAITH}. {WHY}\n\nThe council must say how the colony keeps its faiths.

li.label: Share the {ALTAR}: the faiths take turns
li.outcome: The faiths take turns at the {ALTAR} now: {FAITH} in the evenings, {OTHERFAITH} at first light, the others as they ask. The open-minded call it the fairest thing the council has done in a while. The devout are less sure.

outcomes.li: [b:faith:devout] The faiths take turns at the {ALTAR}. {B_nameDef} keeps {OTHERFAITH}'s hour to the minute, and makes a point of leaving the place cleaner than {B_pronoun} found it.

li.label: A corner for each faith
li.outcome: Each faith has a corner of its own now, to keep as it likes. Nobody is entirely happy and nobody is unhappy, which the council takes as a good sign. A few of them cleared the corners together.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] Each faith has its own corner now, marked with a cloth or a carved post. The colony got on with clearing them out, side by side.

li.label: clearing a corner for each faith
Name {FAITH} the colony's faith
li.outcome: The council has named {FAITH} the colony's faith. Its believers stand a little taller. Everyone else has gone quiet, and some of the devout have gone very quiet indeed.

outcomes.li: [b:faith:devout] The council has named {FAITH} the colony's faith. {B_nameDef} heard it out, said nothing, and went straight to {B_possessive} room.
[b:persona:curious] The council has named {FAITH} the colony's faith. {B_nameDef} took it better than anyone expected, and asked {A_nameDef} where to begin.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has asked the council for an evening to speak for {FAITH}. Whoever wants to come may come, and nobody will be made to. {A_nameDef} says some of the colony have been asking questions.
[persona:warm] {A_nameDef} would like to hold an evening of {FAITH}, with the old stories, for anyone who cares to listen. It would mean a great deal to {A_objective}.
[lowtech] {A_nameDef} asks for an evening by the fire to tell the stories of {FAITH}, the way they were told to {A_objective}.
[faith:alone] {A_nameDef} is the only one of {FAITH} in the colony, and would like one evening to tell the others what {A_pronoun} believes and why.

li.label: Hold the evening, and all are welcome
li.outcome: The council has given {A_nameDef} the evening. {A_nameDef} has gone off to find the right words.

li.label: An evening for those of {FAITH} only
li.outcome: The faithful of {FAITH} keep a quiet evening of their own, and nobody else need hear it. {A_nameDef} says that will do, for now.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: The council said not now. {A_nameDef} nodded and put away the notes {A_pronoun} had been making.
